title: The Girls Who Wanted to Build

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Girls want the builders' advanced lessons, kept for a few apprentices: open the lessons, or set up a new apprenticeship.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and several other girls want to learn how to raise the big roof beams, but the builders only teach that to three apprentices, all chosen by the builders' own families. (friend), a builder, thinks that is unfair, but the other builders disagree. What should (friend) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) opens the lessons to anyone who wants to come. The other builders grumble. Twelve young villagers turn up, (subject) at the front. She is the first to raise a beam on her own.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) starts a second apprenticeship of (friend.his/her) own, for anyone. It takes longer for (subject) to learn, without the best tools. But she does. Eventually, the builders merge the two, because (friend)'s apprentices are better.
